title: Social status and skin health – a cross-sectional study in clinical dermatology
summary:
Our study examines how people's social and economic status, such as education, occupation and income, is related to the occurrence of certain skin diseases. These include open leg wounds (ulcer cruris), infectious skin diseases such as shingles (heroes zoster) or erysipelas and pyoderma, as well as chronic inflammatory skin diseases such as psoriasis and neurodermatitis (atopic dermatitis). We are looking at whether people with different social statuses make use of specific allergy treatments with varying frequency. 

The study is being conducted on adult patients at the Dermatology Clinic of Aachen University Hospital. All participants fill out a standardised questionnaire once, which collects information about their social status, their illness and their quality of life. Participation takes about 10 to 15 minutes and is voluntary. There are no additional medical risks.

The aim is to find out whether and to what extent social factors influence the frequency of skin diseases and the use of medical services. The result should help to better identify risk factors and improve dermatological care in a targeted manner.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age  ≥ 18 years
- Presence of one skin disease (ulcers, herpes zoster, erysipelas, pyoderma, psoriasis or atopic dermatitis) or use of elective allergoloical treatment (exposure testing or hyposensitisation)
- Inpatient or outpatient stay at the Dermatology Clinic, University Hospital Aachen, location: Franziskus
- Capacity to give consent
- Willingness to participate and complete the standardised questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Lack of capacity to give consent 
- Insufficient language skills, if it is not possible to provide information in an understandable form
- Refusal to participate in the study
